title: Emmet County adopts one-year data center moratorium
summary: The Emmet County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to approve a one-year moratorium on data centers. The board cited health concerns, water usage and energy needs and said it wants time to learn more about the effects of a data center.
source_title: KTIV — Emmet County, IA approves one-year data center moratorium
verbatims: The Emmet County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to approve a one-year moratorium on data centers in their Northwest Iowa county.
The board approved the moratorium to allow time to learn more about the possible effects of building a data center, specifically citing health concerns, water usage and energy needs.
notes: Scope (unincorporated vs countywide) not stated in the KTIV article. A Citizen Portal summary cites a 'Resolution 26-25' and rezoning/permit scope; that is an aggregator and was not verified, so it is not used.

title: Taylor County adopts 12-month data center moratorium (pre-window, untracked)

verbatims: The Taylor County Iowa board of supervisors approve a 12 month moratorium on data centers and related businesses.
The ten page document that received a unanimous vote also applies to solar energy systems, battery energy storage systems, and mineral extraction operations.

title: Woodbury County adopts 12-month moratorium on data centers in unincorporated areas (pre-window, untracked)
summary: On June 23, 2026 the Woodbury County supervisors passed a 12-month moratorium on data centers in unincorporated areas, 5-0. The moratorium does not affect existing data centers or approved applications.
source_title: WOWT — Woodbury County passes moratorium on data center projects
verbatims: On Tuesday, June 23, the Woodbury County supervisors passed a 12-month moratorium on potential data centers in unincorporated areas. It passed unanimously, 5-0.
It does not affect any existing data centers or applications that have been approved
notes: PRE-WINDOW (event 2026-06-23). Flagged as untracked and important.

title: Milwaukee Common Council approves one-year data center moratorium

facts.scope: new data centers and expansion of existing facilities; site-specific PDD zoning still possible

summary: The Milwaukee Common Council unanimously approved a one-year moratorium on new data center development on Oct. 13, 2026, to allow time to write permanent zoning rules. The moratorium generally prohibits construction of new data centers or expansion of existing facilities. Developers may still seek site-specific zoning changes.
source_title: Urban Milwaukee — Council Unanimously Approves Data Center Moratorium
verbatims: The Milwaukee Common Council on Tuesday unanimously approved a one-year moratorium on new data center development
The moratorium will expire after one year or upon adoption of permanent regulations, whichever comes first
notes: Event date 2026-10-13 is the Tuesday in the article dated Oct 13, 2026. The probe fetched the ?p=1006567 short link, which redirects to the cited URL. The Walmart/Midtown data-center context in the Hoodline and Urban Milwaukee coverage is not verbatim-checked and is not in the summary.

title: Mount Pleasant Plan Commission approves Microsoft amended site plan (seven buildings, down from nine); village board vote pending

facts.next_step: village board vote expected later in October 2026 (no date stated)

summary: The Mount Pleasant Plan Commission unanimously approved Microsoft's amended site plan on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. The amended plan has seven data center buildings instead of the nine approved in January. Building floor space rises to over 5.8 million square feet. The village board is expected to vote later this month.
source_title: Wisconsin Public Radio — Microsoft planning to build fewer data centers at sprawling Mount Pleasant campus
verbatims: In January, the Mount Pleasant Village Board approved the site plan for the company to build nine data centers
The company is now amending that down to seven data center buildings.
On Wednesday, the Mount Pleasant Plan Commission unanimously approved the amended site plan.
The village board is expected to vote on it later this month.
notes: Event date 2026-10-14 is the Wednesday before the Oct 15, 2026 WPR article. This resolves part of the BACKLOG lead: the Plan Commission approval is verified, but the village board vote is still pending, and no post-vote coverage was found. Recheck the village board October minutes.

title: Dane County Board approves 18-month pause on hyperscale data center permits in unincorporated (county-zoned) towns (pre-window, untracked)

facts.threshold: at least 5,000 servers and at least 10,000 sq ft floor space
facts.scope: towns subject to county zoning; not cities or villages

summary: The Dane County Board approved an 18-month pause on hyperscale data center applications and zoning permits on June 4, 2026. The pause covers towns under county zoning and does not apply to cities or villages. Smaller data center infrastructure is not affected.
source_title: Dane County, WI — Dane County Board Approves 18-Month Pause on Hyperscale Data Center Development
verbatims: Dane County Board Approves 18-Month Pause on Hyperscale Data Center Development
the resolution was narrowed to apply only to hyperscale data centers, defined as facilities that use at least 5,000 servers and occupy at least 10,000 square feet of floor space.
The moratorium applies to towns subject to county zoning.
notes: PRE-WINDOW (event 2026-06-04). Flagged as untracked and important. Board approval is verified. The county executive's signature (WKOW) and the RES-039 number (search only) are NOT verified. The status should stay enacted only if the signature is confirmed.

title: Kiowa County emergency temporary moratorium on data center facility applications, Resolution 2026-4 (pre-window, untracked)

facts.instrument: Resolution No. 2026-4, emergency temporary moratorium on processing applications
facts.scope: data center facilities wholly or partially in unincorporated Kiowa County

summary: Kiowa County's Board of County Commissioners adopted Resolution 2026-4, an emergency temporary moratorium on processing applications for data center facilities in unincorporated Kiowa County, while it revises its regulations. The resolution states a six-month term.

title: Ralls County Commission approves one-year data center moratorium
summary: The Ralls County Commission approved a one-year moratorium on data centers without waiting for a planning and zoning hearing. It halts economic-development applications until September 1, 2027, giving the county time to study the issue and write regulations.
source_title: Muddy River News — Ralls County Commissioners place moratorium on data centers
verbatims: Ralls County Commissioners went ahead and passed a one-year moratorium
The moratorium halts economic-development applications until September 1, 2027, giving the County time to study the issue and develop regulations.
notes: Event date 2026-08-25 is the ARTICLE publication date; the source does not state the meeting date (article says the vote came before a planned September hearing, and social media reacted 'last week'). Confirm the meeting date from Ralls County minutes. Vote tally not stated in the article.

title: Benton County six-month data center moratorium; developer lawsuit and restraining order
summary: Benton County commissioners adopted a six-month data center moratorium in August 2026. A developer sued the commissioners over it, a restraining order was granted Sept. 8, and a judge heard arguments on Sept. 21 on whether the county can enforce the moratorium. The county argues the moratorium should stand because the developer's LLC was not a separate legal entity until Aug. 13.
source_title: KY3 — Judge extends restraining order in Benton County, Mo., data center case
verbatims: The moratorium lasts six months.
The county also argues the moratorium should be valid because NSI6 LLC was not legally its own company until August 13, three days after the moratorium was issued.
A restraining order was granted on Sept. 8.
notes: Event date 2026-08-10 is DERIVED: the article says the company became a separate LLC on Aug 13, 'three days after the moratorium was issued'. The Aug 10 date from search was not directly verified. The article reports a court dispute, not a settled outcome; the restraining-order extension and the Sept 21 hearing outcome are not confirmed.

title: Independence adopts UDO zoning changes for data center and battery storage projects
summary: The Independence City Council unanimously approved zoning changes to its Unified Development Ordinance for data centers and battery energy storage systems on Oct. 5, 2026. The changes follow the July 2026 moratorium on new data center applications. This is a zoning amendment, not a moratorium.
source_title: KSHB 41 — Amid moratorium, Independence passes new rules for data center, BESS zoning
verbatims: After several months of conversation and public hearings, the Independence City Council unanimously approved the changes Oct. 5 to its Unified Development Ordinance, or UDO, related to such projects.
Independence initiated a moratorium on new data center projects, which passed in July
notes: The UDO text itself was not fetched, so its substantive requirements are unverified. The record is a zoning ordinance, so it belongs with local policy, not with the moratorium type. The moratorium status (still running or lifted) is not confirmed.

title: Jackson County Legislature passes 180-day moratorium on data center and BESS land use applications (pre-window, untracked)

title: Jasper County Council approves temporary one-year moratorium on data centers and crypto mining in unincorporated areas

facts.scope: new proposals to build data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations in unincorporated parts of the county

summary: The Jasper County Council unanimously approved a temporary one-year moratorium on new data center and cryptocurrency mining proposals in unincorporated parts of the county on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026. The pause lets staff update zoning and land development rules.
source_title: WTOC — Jasper County Council approves 1-year moratorium on data centers
verbatims: Jasper County Council unanimously approved a temporary one-year moratorium Monday night on new proposals to build data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations in unincorporated parts of the county.
notes: Event date 2026-09-21 is the Monday in the Sept 21, 2026 article. Early-September coverage describes a first reading. WTOC does not say whether the Sept 21 vote was the second or the final reading, so the 'enacted' status is unconfirmed. Confirm with the clerk or minutes. This partly resolves the BACKLOG lead.

title: York County Council adopts nine-month moratorium on new data centers in unincorporated areas (pre-window, untracked)

facts.scope: unincorporated York County; no site plans, special exceptions or conditional use permits for new data centers

summary: York County Council gave final approval on Monday, July 13, 2026 to a nine-month moratorium on new data center development in unincorporated areas, by a 6-0 vote. Pending applications are held in abeyance. Staff must produce a study of noise, groundwater, utility rates and related impacts.
source_title: WRHI — York County Council approves nine month data center moratorium
verbatims: York County Council gave final approval Monday night to a nine month moratorium on new data center development in the county's unincorporated areas, voting 6-0
notes: PRE-WINDOW (event 2026-07-13, Monday before the July 14 article). Flagged as untracked and important. Open issue: whether the QTS York County campus (under construction) falls under the vested-rights exemption. Per WBTV and WSOC, the question is unresolved. The end date 'April 2027' is derived from nine months and is not verified.
